Project Proposal

1) Name

Emerald Ouyang

2) Project Topic/Title

Comparative Analysis of Red and White Wine Quality Prediction Models

3) Inspiration

Explain the reason for your choice of data. Why is it interesting to you? Why do you think it is worth exploring for this project? Include any motivations or background that you believe is relevant. (0.5 points)

This dataset is ideal for exploring wine quality prediction due to its real-world relevance in the wine industry and rich feature set. By comparing red and white wines, we can identify key factors influencing quality and determine whether a single or separate models perform better for each type. The project provides valuable insights for winemakers, enhances machine learning skills, and offers a practical application of predictive analytics in food science.

(2 points)

  • Link: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/186/wine+quality
  • This data source named “Wine Quality” posted on UCI machine learning repository includes 2 datasets both containing the physiochemical factor that affect the quality of wine.
  • there are 1599 observation for the redwine dataset, and 4898 observation for the whitewine dataset.
  • there are 12 variables for both dataset and all 12 are continuous variable
  • there are no missing values, no cleaning/imputiong necessary
  • there are some substantial correlation between density and alcohol, ph and fixed acidity, density and fixed acidity.

5) Questions

Answer the following questions to describe your plan for the project content.

  • Is this a regression or a classification problem?
  • Which variable will be the response and which variables will be your predictors?
  • What is your plan to develop a model? How many models are you planning to train? Note that using a single model with all predictors at once is not acceptable. You need to start with a simple model. Keep adding predictors and observe the changes.
  • How will you explore the non-linearities in the data?
  • Are there any variables that you are planning to exclude from your models? If yes, explain why.
  • How will you evaluate the prediction performance of your models? Justify your choice.
  • How will you perform inference on your models?

(2 points)

  • this is a regression problem, the goal is to predic the exact wine quality score.
  • response var: quality(from 0-10)
  • predictor vars: ‘fixed acidity’, ‘volatile acidity’, ‘citric acid’, ‘residual sugar’, ‘chlorides’, ‘free sulfur dioxide’, ‘total sulfur dioxide’, ‘density’, ‘pH’, ‘sulphates’, ‘alcohol’
  • start with a simple linear regression model using one predictor, then multiple regression model which incrementally add more predictors to observe improvements in model performance. I plan to train separate models for red and white wines to compare their predictive accuracy, then develop a combined model includes color as a predictor to assess and compare with the previous models.
  • use scatterplots and polynomial regression, fit interaction terms to capture feature dependencies
  • no variables to be excluded as all are important factors to access the quality of wine
  • use MSE, RMSE and MAE to evaluate the performance of my models, also compare r-squared to assess the variance of different models.
  • conduct t-test, hypothesis testing, and coefficient analysis which is to use L1 regularization to reduce multicollinearity and identify which factors most strongly influence wine quality.
